title: Ecommerce UX: How to Improve the User Experience (with Examples)
summary: Learn how to optimize your ecommerce UX to reduce checkout friction, increase conversions, and build a seamless shopping experience.
body_markdown:
Ecommerce user experience (UX) is much more than web design. It’s how a user interacts with your online store, from their first visit all the way through their customer journey.


Despite brands spending more on digital ads in 2024,[Contentsquare’s 2025 report](https://contentsquare.com/press/2025-digital-experience-benchmarks/) found that conversion rates have dropped 6.1% year over year. According to the report, brands that are focused on reducing friction in the digital experience have been able to address UX issues like load time frustration.


Ahead, learn how to treat ecommerce UX as a revenue lever, find out where friction usually appears as customers shop online, and create your own practical framework to optimize the user journey on Shopify.


## What is ecommerce user experience?


Ecommerce UX covers every interaction in the[customer journey](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/customer-journey-map-ecommerce) that takes place on your website. This includes homepage navigation,[product discovery](https://www.shopify.com/blog/product-discovery) , checkout, and even post-purchase communication. Brands optimize this user journey to increase conversions and prevent the[friction](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-friction) that causes customers to drop off and abandon their carts.


## Why ecommerce UX matters for conversions and revenue


Ecommerce UX matters because poor customer experiences impact conversion and create drop-offs:


- **Poor UX wastes ad spend.** Cost per visit rose 9%, digital ad spend rose 13.2%, and conversion rates fell 6.1% year over year, according to[Contentsquare’s 2025 report](https://contentsquare.com/press/2025-digital-experience-benchmarks/) . If you pay per click and the website experience fails to satisfy, those visitors might exit.
- [Retargeting](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/62605443-how-to-execute-an-effective-ad-retargeting-campaign-that-works) **isn’t foolproof.** Just[13% of visitors](https://contentsquare.com/guides/digital-experience-benchmark/) return within 30 days after their initial visit. Strong ecommerce UX keeps visitors on your site so you don’t have to try to win them back.
- **Checkout optimization drives sales.** Baymard found that 18% of carts are abandoned because the checkout was too long or complicated. (BODi recorded a[10% lift in checkout conversion](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/bodi) after adopting Shopify.)


“We pay attention to every detail—even the font size on the inside of the packaging, or this little phrase,” says Mark Rushmore, co-founder of[SURI](https://www.trysuri.com/) , in a[Shopify Masters interview](https://www.shopify.com/blog/suri-scaling-and-changing-consumer-habits) . In just two years, the toothbrush brand scaled to $30 million in sales by creating a compelling brand story and focusing on customer paint points.


“It’s almost invisible to the naked eye, but it’s the culmination of all those little tiny decisions across packaging, across your checkout, across the whole user experience, which add up to people having a really great experience because they can see and appreciate the detail and thought that’s gone into a lot of small decisions.”

## The core pillars of a strong ecommerce UX


Clear navigation, fast product discovery, detailed product pages, mobile usability, seamless checkout, and personalization are the core pillars of a positive user experience. Here’s how to optimize each for your ecommerce website:


### Clear navigation and information architecture


Shopify’s[navigation menus](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/online-store/menus-and-links) let you maintain cleaner architecture without custom development. You can combine this with[smart collections](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/products/collections/smart-collections) that automatically add or remove products to product categories when certain criteria is met.


[Everlast](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/everlast) , for example, helps online shoppers find what they’re looking for with:


- **Clear navigation labels.** Visitors can choose the broader category (“Equipment”), refine it by sport, then choose a product type to browse.
- **Category structures that reflect how shoppers think.** Everlast groups punch mitts, body protectors, and corner supplies under a single “MMA Coaching Equipment” category.
- **Navigation menus are optimized for mobile devices.** Mobile users see a hamburger menu that shows only the main options to reduce overwhelm.


Everlast’s Shopify-powered store uses clear architecture and navigation menus.


### Faster product discovery with search, filters, and sorting


[Attentive’s 2026 report](https://www.attentive.com/blog/2026-personalization-trends) found that 70% of shoppers say they feel overwhelmed, uncertain, or that it takes too long to find an option they like when shopping online. When they feel this way, 38% postpone purchases for later, while 21% give up searching entirely.


[Decked](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/decked) uses the Shopify[Search & Discovery app](https://apps.shopify.com/search-and-discovery) to aid product discovery. They’ve recorded a 4% revenue lift through features like:


- **Filters and sorting.** Decked built custom filters for product type and compatibility. Shoppers can use the search bar and sort by relevance, or order products from lowest to highest.
- **Search results relevance.** Website visitors can use Decked’s site search to find specific products. Synonym groups created within the Search & Discovery app connect two words with similar meanings.
- **Personalized recommendations.** Business-to-business (B2B) buyers can use Decked’s integrated custom dealer locator if they’d rather shop in-person. “We can match dealers not just by proximity and location, but also based on those who have our product displays or only carry specific items from our range,” says Taylor Straley, VP of ecommerce.


### Product pages that reduce hesitation


Easy product comparison is the reason why[30% of shoppers](https://www.salsify.com/hubfs/2026/Salsify%202026%20Consumer%20Research%20Report%20What%20Makes%20Shopping%20Experiences%20Matter.pdf?hsCtaTracking=29f1f716-1ddf-44a9-9278-23a8be22276a%7C2b9cf60f-067c-41a2-999a-dedf35104d20) said they choose to shop online instead of in-store. You can speak to those visitors by answering buying questions alongside[product descriptions](https://www.shopify.com/blog/8211159-9-simple-ways-to-write-product-descriptions-that-sell) .


Include everything a buyer might look for on a product page, such as:


- High-quality images and videos
- Clear pricing
- Variant options
- Availability or shipping clarity
- [Reviews](https://www.shopify.com/blog/review-generation) or trust cues
- Technical specifications
- Returns information


Shopify brands can use metafields, media support, product variants, subscriptions/apps, and product page flexibility in Shopify themes to present information clearly at scale.


[Shock Surplus](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/shock-surplus) , for example, embeds videos and customer reviews to help customers make purchasing decisions. Rich media can demystify complex products while also guiding shoppers towards potential upgrades.


“We’re enthusiasts, just like our customers, sharing our learnings to make complex products understandable,” says founder and CEO Sean Reyes. This approach has helped position the brand as a trusted resource in the industry.


Shock Surplus has a “select your vehicle” widget and links to buyer’s guides to improve conversion on ecommerce product pages.


### Mobile-first usability


Mobile devices account for[71% of all orders](https://www.statista.com/statistics/568684/e-commerce-website-visit-and-orders-by-device/?srsltid=AfmBOorTbPE1eXxCWvg0b7j8SjsexRTfA7cAYHHLdBi95JFZgSB9DpZf) on ecommerce sites globally. Yet[Baymard found](https://baymard.com/blog/mobile-ux-ecommerce) that 81% of leading ecommerce sites had “mediocre” or worse mobile UX performance.


Consider running a mobile[conversion rate optimization (CRO) audit](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ecommerce-cro-audit) to find out where smartphone shoppers drop off your ecommerce website. Address potential root causes through[ecommerce UX design](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ux-design-trends) best practices like:


- Thumb-friendly navigation
- Tap targets
- Fast load times and site speed
- Stable layouts
- Responsive design


Checkout is a prime area for mobile site optimization. Include only essential information you need to process orders:[Baymard’s study](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate) shows most checkouts can cut the number of form fields by up to 60%.


Premium menswear brand[Serge Blanco](https://sergeblanco.com/en) found this issue with their old platform. “We were seeing significant conversion loss, particularly on mobile, where the checkout funnel lacked fluidity," says Matthieu De Vaulx, traffic manager.


[Serge Blanco replatformed to Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/serge-blanco) to simplify operations, improve performance, and give their team full autonomy. They adopted[Shopify Checkout](https://www.shopify.com/checkout) and immediately removed the friction that had slowed down previous mobile shoppers. “What changed very quickly was how simple checkout became. That drove conversion rates up directly, especially on mobile,” says Julien Fournier, director of ecommerce.


### Checkout that removes friction


Customers who reach the checkout stage show intent to buy, making ecommerce UX even more crucial.


Address common reasons for cart abandonment, per[Baymard](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate) :


- **Extra costs too high.** Use[dynamic tax-inclusive pricing](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/international/pricing/dynamic-tax-inclusive-pricing) and consider[buy now, pay later (BNPL)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/buy-now-pay-later) options for price-conscious shoppers. “[Shop Pay Installments](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/payments/shop-pay-installments) offered our customers a reliable way to upgrade confidently,” says Sean of Shock Surplus. “As soon as we launched them, our average order value jumped 10%.”
- **Slow delivery.**[Parachute](https://parachutehome.com/) lets customers buy online and pickup in-store (BOPIS) to combat slow shipping speeds. They processed[1,300 BOPIS orders in one quarter](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/parachute) —a key part of their migration to Shopify that unlocked more than $1 million in annual operational cost savings.
- **Lack of customer trust.** Show multiple payment options, including local payment methods for international shoppers. Combine this with[social proof](https://www.shopify.com/blog/social-proof) and[user-generated content (UGC)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/user-generated-content) at checkout. Aviator Nation, for example,[integrated Yotpo](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/aviator-nation) to display reviews inside Shopify Checkout.
- **Long, complex checkout process.** Enable autofill and accept digital wallets that already have existing customers’ shipping and payment data stored.


Shopify’s[Checkout Extensibility](https://shopify.dev/changelog/introducing-checkout-extensibility) lets you build upon the[world’s highest-converting checkout](https://www.shopify.com/checkout) . Monos uses it to upsell related products and shipping insurance that seamlessly integrate with[Shop Pay](https://shop.app/shop-pay) . The result: a checkout experience that[converts up to 50% better](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/monos) than guest checkout.


Monos customizes Shopify Checkout to share social proof and upsell shipping protection.


### Personalization without overload


An[Attentive survey](https://www.attentive.com/blog/2026-personalization-trends#toc-1) shows that 64% of shoppers want marketing to be more personalized. Yet[Gartner’s own survey says](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-06-03-gartner-survey-reveals-personalization-can-triple-the-likelihood-of-customer-regret-at-key-journey-points) that 53% of customers had negative experiences with personalization, and those customers were 44% less likely to purchase again.


Privacy is one of the concerns at play. Attentive found that 71% of customers actively take steps to protect their privacy, and 42% think it feels uncomfortable or invasive when brands personalize in a way it knows something the shopper never shared.


[First- and zero-party data](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/zero-party-data-vs-first-party-data) address these concerns:


How it’s collected Data sources Data to collect Personalization example


Zero-party data Shared directly by your customers Quizzes, user feedback surveys, polls, support tickets, and wish lists Interests, preferences, goals, and purchase intentions[Ruggable’s “Rug Quiz”](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/ruggable) asks customers to choose the designs they like and uses this to personalize product recommendations


[First-party data](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/first-party-data) Sourced from owned channels Website analytics tools, point-of-sale (POS) systems, email marketing tools, customer loyalty programs, and pixel data Purchase history, items returned, retail store visits, loyalty points earned, and pages viewed[Pura Vida](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/pura-vida-bracelets) uses customer history to personalize emails in automated sequences


Shopify lets you scale personalized ecommerce UX strategies with[unified customer profiles](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/unified-customer-profiles) . These profiles power[dynamic segments](https://www.shopify.com/segmentation) you can use to personalize outreach through[Shopify Messaging](https://www.shopify.com/email-marketing) , as well as personalization apps like[Nosto](https://apps.shopify.com/nosto-personalization-for-shopify) .


[Creality](https://www.creality.com/) leaned on Shopify to consolidate their global direct-to-consumer (DTC) network with localized ecommerce storefronts, local payments, and centralized operations. This included Shop app, which allows them to automate personalized notifications for global shoppers.


“Other platforms help you reach customers, but they make it hard to build real relationships or access the data you need,” says sales director Eva Hu. “Our goal was to create lasting brand loyalty, not just complete transactions.”


Since migrating,[Creality recorded a 20% increase in sitewide conversion](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/creality) and seven times return on ad spend from Shop app campaigns.

## Ecommerce UX examples


Draw inspiration from these ecommerce brands who lean on Shopify features to improve their ecommerce UX:


### Dermalogica


[Dermalogica](https://www.dermalogica.com/) proved that UX gains often come from improving team speed and maintainability, not just changing visuals.


Their previous theme had become 60% custom code. It slowed iteration and created developer bottlenecks—building templates, adding fields, and tweaking page layouts—that took time away from innovation.


Dermalogica switched to[Shopify’s Horizon theme](https://themes.shopify.com/themes/horizon/presets/horizon) foundation and used native settings, blocks, and AIassisted prototyping to reduce dependency on custom development. The result:[9% lift in ecommerce store conversion](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/dermalogica-horizon-theme) , 12% faster page load times, 40% less developer maintenance time, and roughly $39,000 in annual savings.


### Faherty


Better discovery and faster merchandising execution can translate directly into revenue.[Faherty](https://fahertybrand.com/) is a great example; their previous ecommerce foundation limited performance during peak periods and product launches.


As they[replatformed to Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/faherty) , Faherty worked with Shopify Plus partner[Verbal+Visual](https://www.shopify.com/partners/directory/partner/verbalplusvisual) to redesign their site. They deployed:


- AI-powered product discovery tools
- Quick add buttons on product cards
- Persistent flyout cart
- Composable design with modular content blocks


Faherty’s new site design contributed to a[28% revenue increase](https://www.shopify.com/case-studies/faherty) and a 15% increase in search-referrer conversion. “The new site has dramatically improved our shopping experience and helped us get ahead of trends and seasonal opportunities instead of reacting to them,” says founder and CEO Alex Faherty.

## Ecommerce UX FAQ


### Why is ecommerce UX important for conversions?


Ecommerce UX is important for conversions because friction can cause people to exit your website. Take the checkout experience:[Baymard found](https://baymard.com/lists/cart-abandonment-rate) that 70% of all carts are abandoned. The biggest drivers were high extra costs and slow delivery. Test UX improvements—like inclusive pricing, free shipping offers, or expedited shipping options—to monitor the impact on conversions.


### How can Shopify improve ecommerce UX?


Shopify helps brands improve their ecommerce UX with platform features like:


- Guest checkout options
- One-page checkout via[Shop Pay](https://shop.app/shop-pay)
- [Search & Discovery app](https://apps.shopify.com/search-and-discovery)
- Metafields and metaobjects
- Theme editor and app blocks


### What’s the difference between ecommerce UX and ecommerce CX?


Ecommerce UX focuses on the user experience someone has on your website. Ecommerce customer experience (CX) is broader and covers every interaction a customer has with your brand, including on your website, the product and shipping experience, returns handling, and customer service interactions.


### How often should an ecommerce business audit its UX?


The review cadence for an ecommerce UX audit depends on factors like traffic volume, platform, catalog complexity, and how quickly your website changes. A small retail store might review their UX monthly; an enterprise brand might opt for an “always on” approach to reduce friction, especially on websites where small conversion gains result in large revenue uplifts.
